info.title: API.SH: Google Finance
info.description: The Google Finance API from API.SH: public Google Finance data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: Fetch a past response again, free
get.description: The exact response a call returned, for 30 days after the call, at no cost. Use the call's x-request-id. Supports output=csv|ndjson.

200.description: The stored response (headers: x-refetch: 1, x-original-time, x-original-route).

404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

get.description:
Each point has its time (with the market's UTC offset), price, change and change % against the chart's reference price (the previous close for 1d, the first point otherwise) and volume where the market reports it.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-chart

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: TICKER:EXCHANGE as Google Finance writes it, e.g. `AAPL:NASDAQ`, `VOD:LON`, `.INX:INDEXSP`; a currency or crypto pair such as `EUR-USD` or `BTC-USD`. A bare US ticker such as `AAPL` is looked up on the US exchanges.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: The chart range (default 1m).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Interface language, e.g. `en` (default).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Up to 20 live quotes side by side (stocks, ETFs, indexes, currencies, crypto): price, change, change %, previous close, after-hours, currency and update time, plus the best and worst performer of the day. Bare tickers are matched to their main listing; symbols not found come back with found=false.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-compare

parameters.name: symbols
parameters.description: Comma-separated: AAPL:NASDAQ, MSFT, .INX:INDEXSP, EUR-USD, BTC-USD ...

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Live crypto quotes: price, change and change %, previous close, update time, base and quote names, for one or several pairs. Without a symbol: the crypto board of the Google Finance home page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-crypto

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Comma-separated pairs (BTC-USD, ETH-EUR) or coins with currency.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Quote currency for bare coins (default USD).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The live exchange rate of a currency pair: rate, change and change % since the previous close, previous close, update time, inverse rate, both currency names, and an amount converted.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-currency

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: Currency pair: EUR-USD, EURUSD or EUR/USD.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Base currency (with to) instead of pair.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Quote currency (with from).

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount of the base currency to convert.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A company's financial statements from Google Finance, quarterly or annual: for each period (label, fiscal year and quarter, period end date, currency) the income statement (revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, R&D, SG&A, operating expense, total expenses, operating income, EBITDA, other non-operating income, pre-tax income, income tax, effective tax rate, net income, net profit margin, EPS diluted and basic), balance sheet (cash, short-term investments, receivables, inventory, current and total assets, PP&E, long-term investments, payables, short-term and long-term debt, deferred revenue, current and total liabilities, retained earnings, accumulated other comprehensive income, total equity, shares outstanding, price to book) and cash flow (net income, cash from operations, capital expenditure, cash from investing, dividends paid, stock issued or repurchased, cash from financing, net change in cash, free cash flow). Values are in the reporting currency; percentages as numbers.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-financials

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: TICKER:EXCHANGE as Google Finance writes it, e.g. `AAPL:NASDAQ`, `MSFT:NASDAQ`, `VOD:LON`, `RELIANCE:NSE`. A bare US ticker such as `AAPL` is looked up on the US exchanges.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: quarterly (default; the latest quarters) or annual (the latest fiscal years).

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Comma-separated statements to return: income_statement, balance_sheet, cash_flow (default all three).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Interface language, e.g. `en` (default).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The Google Finance home page as data: the AI market summary (headlines with their cited articles), the market boards (US or North America, Europe, Asia or India, Latin America indexes, currencies, crypto, futures: price, change, % change, previous close, update time), top movers (gainers, losers, most active, with after-hours prices), sector lists (open, high, low), upcoming earnings (date, time, EPS and revenue estimates) and market news (title, source, snippet, thumbnail, tickers). `gl` picks the market: movers, news, earnings, the local index board, currency pairs and the summary follow it (e.g. `gl=IN` gives NSE/BSE movers and INR pairs).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-markets

parameters.name: gl
parameters.description: Market country, default US (two letters: US, IN, DE, GB, JP, ...).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Language, default en (the market summary is written in it).

parameters.name: movers
parameters.description: Top movers per list (gainers, losers, most active), default 10, max 50.

parameters.name: news
parameters.description: News stories, default 20 (Google returns up to ~30).

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Comma list of the parts to return: summary, indexes, movers, lists, earnings, news (default all). Fewer sections make the call smaller and faster.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Google Finance news for a stock
get.description:
News about a stock, ETF or index from its Google Finance page: headline, link, source, publish time, summary, image, source icon and the other symbols each story mentions. Headlines and links only, not full articles.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-news

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: TICKER:EXCHANGE as Google Finance writes it, e.g. `AAPL:NASDAQ`, `TSLA:NASDAQ`, `.INX:INDEXSP`. A bare US ticker such as `AAPL` is looked up on the US exchanges.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum stories (1-50, default 50).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Interface language, e.g. `en` (default).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A stock, index, currency or crypto quote as Google Finance shows it: price, change, day range, market cap, volume, P/E, dividend, 52-week range, EPS, beta, shares, employees, CEO, founded, headquarters and the analyst outlook. Also returns market_status (e.g. With window, price_series adds the chart for that range (points with time, price, change and volume, a summary, and after-hours points on 1d).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-quote

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: TICKER or TICKER:EXCHANGE (AAPL:NASDAQ, TSLA, BTC-USD, .INX:INDEXSP).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Language, default en.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Adds price_series for this chart range: 1d, 5d, 1m, 6m, ytd, 1y, 5y or max.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The tickers Google Finance lists as related to a quote (people also search for), each with its live quote.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-related

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: TICKER:EXCHANGE, a bare ticker, a currency or crypto pair, or a Google Finance quote link.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many (default 10, max 20).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Find stocks, ETFs, funds, indexes, currencies and crypto pairs by name or ticker, each with its live quote: symbol, exchange, full ticker (TICKER:EXCHANGE), name, type, currency, price, change and change %, previous close, after-hours price, update time, time zone and country.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-finance-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name or ticker words.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Keep one type only.

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Language (default en).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
